import ast
import operator

def evaluate(node, user):
    if isinstance(node, ast.BoolOp):
        values = [evaluate(v, user) for v in node.values]
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.And):
            return all(values)
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Or):
            return any(values)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
        value = evaluate(node.operand, user)
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Not):
            return not value
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
        left = evaluate(node.left, user)
        # Assuming only one operator for Compare based on typical filter strings
        # A more complex case would be 1 < x < 3, but let's stick to what's requested
        # Actually the prompt says "id > 1 and email != 'x@y.org'"
        # Comparing two values:
        right = evaluate(node.comparators[0], user)
        op = node.ops[0]
        if isinstance(op, ast.Eq): return left == right
        if isinstance(op, ast.NotEq): return left != right
        if isinstance(op, ast.Lt): return left < right
        if isinstance(op, ast.LtE): return left <= right
        if isinstance(op, ast.Gt): return left > right
        if isinstance(op, ast.GtE): return left >= right
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Constant):
        return node.value
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Name):
        if node.id in user:
            return user[node.id]
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown field: {node.id}")
    
    raise ValueError("Unsupported expression")

print(evaluate(tree.body, user))

expr = "id > 1 and email != 'x@y.org'"
tree = ast.parse(expr, mode='eval')
print(evaluate(tree.body, user))

from app.api.handlers import handle_filter_users

def test_filter_users():
    # Valid filters
    assert handle_filter_users({"where": "name == 'Ada'"}) == (200, {"users": [{"id": 1, "name": "Ada", "email": "ada@example.com"}]})
    assert handle_filter_users({"where": "id > 1"}) == (200, {"users": [{"id": 2, "name": "Linus", "email": "linus@example.com"}]})
    assert handle_filter_users({"where": "id >= 1 and email != 'x@y.org'"}) == (200, {"users": [
        {"id": 1, "name": "Ada", "email": "ada@example.com"},
        {"id": 2, "name": "Linus", "email": "linus@example.com"}
    ]})
    
    # Invalid filters
    assert handle_filter_users({}) == (400, {"error": "invalid filter"})
    assert handle_filter_users({"where": 123}) == (400, {"error": "invalid filter"})
    assert handle_filter_users({"where": "len(name) > 0"}) == (400, {"error": "invalid filter"})
    assert handle_filter_users({"where": "name.upper() == 'ADA'"}) == (400, {"error": "invalid filter"})
    assert handle_filter_users({"where": "id + 1 == 2"}) == (400, {"error": "invalid filter"})

test_filter_users()
